newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-British papers hail 'lame duck' Morrison.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-British papers hail 'lame duck' Morrison.

text.p: The legend of Danny Morrison, world's cricket's lame duck batsman defying England's attack gathered pace on Wednesday, English cricket's more vocal critics were calling for heads to roll at the latest failure by the national team.

Morrison's defiant final wicket stand with Nathan Astle to save the first test in Auckland has captured the imagination of the British media, with The Times in an editorial today calling the New Zealand No.11 "a hero for all underdogs matched against hopeless odds".

And, perhaps overestimating the Classical knowledge of New Zealand cricket fans, it added: "For the carousers in the club bars of New Zealand, Danny Morrison's last stand will today rank in history with such epic feats as Horatius holding the bridge and Roland blocking the pass.
"Morrison's bulldog determination to play each ball on its merits, to look certain defeat in the eyes and stare it down, and never to surrender are lessons to relish everywhere."
The Times headed its back sports page with a graphic of 24 ducks, representing his 24 test noughts, but with a swan at the end representing his latest innings.
It headed its story: "The day England turned cricket's ugly duck king into a swan".
The Guardian called Morrison "a bunny with bottle", while the Daily Mail dubbed Morrison's test record "a real quacker".

Meanwhile, England's failure to press home their advantage on the last day has led to inevitable calls to sack skipper Mike Atherton. Significantly, the calls have come from figures outside the game, and safely ensconced in an English winter.
Ray Illingworth, who stood down as England's chairman of selectors at the end of last season, laid the blame at Atherton's feet, but reserved special criticism for bowling coach Ian Botham.
"Mike Atherton must take much of the blame for England's unbelievable failure to beat New Zealand yesterday," Illingworth wrote in the Express.
"His lacklustre, unimaginative captaincy, along with some awful bowling, lay at the heart of another alarming tour debacle."
Illingworth said Atherton did not set the correct fields to Morrison, crowding the bat to pressurise him, and failed to take advantage of having five bowlers.
He said the England skipper should not be written off but was now under immense pressure.
Botham, too, must answer questions, said Illingworth, after the poor bowling display.

He said England's bowlers should put more thought into their play: "That is where technical adviser Ian Botham ought to be making an impact. But maybe he's not as good as he thought he was, maybe he's not finding it as easy a job as he thought it
would be.
"I can't say I'm surprised by that."
Not surprisingly, the tabloid Sun and Mirror were much more direct.
"Atherton must go -- NOW!" shouted the Sun, with the Mirror adding: "Get out now Ath".
A Sun editorial said bluntly: "The England cricket team is a joke -- it couldn't beat an egg.
"There's only one solution. Atherton must Ath-ter-go."
